account: Today I read my appointment book and attended the ten o'clock market walk. I am now at home early for my noon lunch, with accounts at the office at one, tea at an unspecified east-bank dockside cottage at three, and office time at four-thirty. The secretary could not identify the tea host from the book. The builder is seeking an agreed repair scope and payment and says he has planks and lanterns ready. I asked him to bring a proposal at one and not begin paid work before terms are recorded; I have not yet received specific reports of damage. Market conversations have yielded little concrete news. Several townsfolk reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery, then bread near the inn. I personally saw the baker carrying a sack of bread by the market and putting bread into the bakery stall chest. That looks consistent with baking and restocking for customers, not clear evidence of anything unusual. I heard indistinct speech from freight and later from the baker, including a distant shout, but could not understand it and cannot say what it concerned. My attempts to speak to freight apparently went unheard despite his appearing nearby. I do not currently have evidence of an unusual event or a hidden purpose involving anyone.
